chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: The people of Makkah objected to you that you slaughtered your sacrificial offering in your house in Makkah. So he said: Indeed, all of Makkah is a place of slaughter.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to a sacrificial offering that is not obligatory, for that may be slaughtered in Makkah, as was explained in detail in the first report.

key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering, especially in legal discussion of hajj
key_terms.بِوَاجِبٍ: not obligatory; referring to a non-mandatory offering
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city discussed here as a valid place of slaughter in this context
key_terms.مَنْحَرٌ: a place of slaughter for sacrificial animals
key_terms.هَدْيَكَ: your sacrificial offering brought for hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Can a sacrificial offering be slaughtered in one's house in Makkah during hajj?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on where a sacrificial offering may be slaughtered during hajj. The Imam عليه السلام states that all of Makkah is a place of slaughter, and the report is understood as referring to a non-obligatory offering, since the obligatory hady has a more specific legal ruling.
